tagline: Okinawa's beach-perfect island group — a million-plus visitors, a booming cruise port, Japan's largest coral reef offshore, and no modern water mobility at all.
summary: Miyakojima is the flat, reef-ringed beach capital of Okinawa's outer islands: Yonaha Maehama's 7 km of white sand, the Shigira resort coast, Irabu and Shimoji across the famous 3,540 m Irabu Bridge, and the Yabiji reef complex — Japan's largest coral reef group — just north of Ikema. Arrivals first broke one million in FY2018 and Hirara has been built up as an international cruise hub. Notably, the islands' last scheduled ferries were replaced by the bridge in 2015 — so unlike most of Okinawa there is almost no boat service left, even as visitor numbers and cruise calls climb. The water is the unused asset; reef day-trips, resort transfers and cross-archipelago line-hauls are the network to build.

demand_signals.label: Visitor arrivals
demand_signals.value: 1.14M in FY2018 — first time over 1M, fifth straight record
demand_signals.note: Driven by new direct flights, the Shimojishima airport reopening (2019) and cruise growth; monthly arrivals in late 2025 were running ~100k+ — a sustained million-plus market.
demand_signals.source: Miyakojima City tourism statistics / Yaeyama Nippo

demand_signals.label: Cruise-port growth at Hirara
demand_signals.note: Hirara was designated an international cruise hub port under a public-private development scheme — thousands of passengers per call who currently disperse by bus, with no water-side excursion product.
demand_signals.source: Okinawa Prefecture cruise statistics / Hirara Port studies

demand_signals.label: Japan's largest coral reef group
demand_signals.note: The premier snorkel/dive destination reachable only by small charter boats on calm days; a clean, quiet, shallow-draft foiling platform is the conservation-aligned way to open it reliably.

demand_signals.label: The bridge that ended the ferries
demand_signals.value: Irabu Ōhashi (3,540 m, 2015) — Japan's longest toll-free bridge
demand_signals.note: The Hirara↔Irabu ferries were withdrawn the day the bridge opened — proof the corridor carried scheduled marine traffic within the decade, and the reason the islands now have no boat network even as tourism has doubled.
demand_signals.source: ANA Japan Travel Planner / Miyakojima City

use_cases.title: Yabiji reef day-trips
use_cases.body: Scheduled foiling departures from Hirara to the Yabiji reef complex (~10 nm) — smooth, shallow-draft, zero-emission access to Japan's largest coral reef group, replacing weather-limited small charters with a reliable premium product.

use_cases.title: Cruise-passenger excursion fleet
use_cases.body: Hirara's cruise calls deliver thousands of passengers per ship with nowhere to go on the water — foiling shuttles to Yabiji, the Shigira coast and around the bridge islands turn port calls into marine revenue at N35 Shuttle capacity.

use_cases.title: Resort-coast transfers
use_cases.body: Direct hops linking Hirara, the Shigira resort zone (~5 nm), and Iraph SUI on Irabu (~6 nm) — a water-side arrival and inter-resort tier for the islands' premium properties.

use_cases.title: Cross-archipelago line-hauls
use_cases.body: Naha ↔ Miyako (~155 nm) and Miyako ↔ Ishigaki (~70–80 nm) are air-only today — Quanta-LR hybrid legs put Miyako on the prefecture's surface network with no island charging dependency.

journeys.today: Small charter boats on calm days only; the reef group — Japan's largest — is effectively closed in chop and has no scheduled access.
journeys.with_navier: A smooth foiling run that flies above the swell, opening reliable, low-wake, zero-emission reef days over the 'eighth continent' of coral.

journeys.today: A taxi over the bridge — scenic, but the marine arrival vanished with the 2015 ferry withdrawal.
journeys.with_navier: A ~6 nm foiling transfer revives the water approach as the premium arrival for the bridge islands' luxury properties.

journeys.today: Road transfer around the island's southern shore; the resorts' sea frontage is unused for mobility.
journeys.with_navier: A short coastal glide delivering guests from port or cruise ship straight to the resort waterfront.

journeys.today: Air-only — no surface link between Okinawa's two southern archipelagos.
journeys.with_navier: A ~70–80 nm Quanta-LR hybrid line-haul connects the beach islands to the Yaeyama wilderness mesh — one network across the prefecture's south.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Everything local is short and all-electric: Yabiji ~10 nm, Irabu/Iraph SUI ~6 nm, Shigira ~5 nm, east-coast and Ikema hops all <15 nm — flat-water, reef-fringed geography where shallow draft and zero wake matter. Miyako's grid (and the Shimoji/Irabu redevelopment zone) supports shore charging.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Miyako's links to the rest of the prefecture are explicitly hybrid: Naha ↔ Miyako ~155 nm and Miyako ↔ Ishigaki ~70–80 nm by sea (just past the all-electric edge). Both are air-only today — Quanta-LR adds the surface spine without any outer-island charging infrastructure.

competitive_landscape: Miyako is the rare island destination with almost no incumbent on the water: the Hirara↔Irabu ferries were withdrawn when the Irabu Bridge opened in 2015, leaving only small dive/charter operators and glass-bottom boats. Meanwhile demand has compounded — million-plus annual arrivals, a purpose-built international cruise berth at Hirara, and a resort buildout from Shigira to Irabu. The withdrawn-ferry history proves marine service worked here; the cruise and resort growth proves the demand returned bigger than the boats. Inter-island flows to Naha and Ishigaki run entirely on JTA/RAC aircraft.

precedents.why_it_matters: Flat reef-lagoon geography, resort jetties and short hops — the Maldives operating template matches Miyako's water almost exactly.

seasonality: Typhoon season (Jun–Oct) brings the hard stops; the NE winter monsoon (Nov–Mar) puts chop on the exposed north side — exactly what keeps small charters away from Yabiji much of the year. The lagoon and south-coast legs stay operable nearly year-round, and foiling above the swell widens the Yabiji window substantially. Peak beach season (Apr–Oct) aligns with the calmest inshore water outside typhoon passages.
regulatory_note: Pier jurisdiction sits with Miyakojima City and Hirara Port's public-private international cruise-hub framework, under JCG 11th Regional HQ (Naha) and MLIT Kyushu. The Yabiji reef group is a protected natural monument area where wake, anchor and emissions discipline is a permitting advantage for clean foiling fleets. The Shimoji/Irabu post-bridge redevelopment (including the reopened Shimojishima airport) is an open design-in window for water-side infrastructure — aligned with Japan's 2050 carbon-neutrality target.
